common.disclaimer: Fodmara is a self-observation diary, not a medical device. It does not diagnose and gives no diet or treatment advice. Talk to your doctor or dietitian about what you log.

gutScale.question: How is your gut today?
gutScale.infoWhat: Rate your gut symptoms for the day as a whole – bloating, pain, gas, an urgent or stuck bowel – not the worst moment (that is what a flare-up is for). The number is yours: compare it with your own days.
infoScale: 1–3 – there, but it doesn't change your day
7–8 – bad, it gets in the way
9–10 – as bad as it ever gets
gutScale.infoTip: Check in at about the same time every evening. Bloating and pain are logged separately because they often move differently.

redFlags.link: When should I see a doctor?
redFlags.title: When to see a doctor
redFlags.intro: IBS is uncomfortable but not dangerous. Some symptoms are not typical of IBS and should be checked:
redFlags.urgentTitle: Same day – or call emergency services
urgent: Heavy bleeding from the bottom, black or tarry stools, or vomiting blood.
Sudden, severe belly pain that does not ease, or pain with a high fever.
You cannot pass stool or wind and your belly is swelling, with vomiting.
soon: Symptoms that wake you at night.
A lasting change in bowel habits, especially if you are over 50.
Family history of bowel or ovarian cancer, coeliac disease or inflammatory bowel disease.
Tiredness with low iron or anaemia, or a fever that keeps coming back.
Bloating that is there almost every day for weeks (especially for women over 50).
redFlags.routine: If your IBS has been diagnosed and nothing above applies, low-FODMAP is best done with a dietitian. Your doctor can refer you.
redFlags.disclaimer: General information, not a diagnosis. If in doubt, call your doctor.

stool.title: Toilet visit

typeLong.1: separate hard lumps, hard to pass
typeLong.3: like a sausage with cracks on the surface
typeLong.6: fluffy, mushy pieces with ragged edges

stool.bloodTitle: Blood in your stool should be checked
stool.bloodBody: Book an appointment with your doctor. Heavy bleeding or black stools: seek help the same day. Tap for more.
stool.infoWhat: Doctors and dietitians use the Bristol stool scale to describe stool consistency without awkward words. Type 3–4 is usually considered normal; 1–2 points to slow transit, 5–7 to fast.
stool.infoTip: Log what you see right after a visit – memory gets fuzzy by evening.

foods.title: Foods
foods.intro: Which FODMAP groups a food typically contains. The amount matters a lot – many foods are fine in small portions.
foods.disclaimer: General information from public sources, not a personal diet. Your dietitian decides what and how much.
foods.settingsHint: Which FODMAP groups common foods contain

fodmap.infoWhat: FODMAPs are carbohydrates that some people absorb poorly. In the gut they draw in water and are fermented, which can cause bloating, pain and diarrhoea or constipation in people with IBS. There are six groups:
phases: Elimination: 2–6 weeks with few FODMAPs, to see if symptoms improve.
Reintroduction: test one group at a time – small, medium, large portion over three days, then a pause.
Personalisation: eat as varied as you can, limiting only what you react to.
fodmap.infoTip: Low-FODMAP is not meant to be a diet for life. A dietitian helps you do it safely and get as much variety back as possible.
fodmap.infoDisclaimer: General information, not a diet plan. Fodmara does not use or show any official FODMAP measurements.

test.notePh: e.g. fine with a slice, bloated with two
